Subject: Export compliance checklist and subprocessor affirmations

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday — Medixa is excited about Redwood's throughput profile. Legal has asked me to collect a short evidence pack so we can move the procurement review forward. At a high level they need: 

- Confirmation that Redwood relies on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and whether a UK IDTA / UK Addendum is available for UK data subjects.
- A current subprocessor register scoped to production inference (including regions where data may transit or be processed).
- Any completed or draft TIAs / DTIA-style technical assessments you have for EU->US/UK transfers (summary is fine).
- Copy of the executed SCCs or a redline-friendly draft and your proposed next steps for signature (DocuSign is preferred).

I've attached a simple checklist for our legal ops team (evidence_checklist.xlsx) to help structure the deliverables. The procurement timeline is tight — can you confirm whether you can provide the pack by EOD Friday (30 Apr)? If not, please propose a realistic date and a short plan for missing items.

Also: a couple of questions from our security reviewer (cc'd):
- Do any subprocessors store unredacted customer data outside the EU/UK?
- Are you able to provide a minimal data flow diagram that highlights cross-border hops for inference requests?

Looking forward to your reply.

Best,
Sasha Turner
Head of Integrations, Medixa
Sasha.turner@medixa.com

Attachment: evidence_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

Sasha — thanks, and great to meet yesterday. We're happy to move quickly on this. High-level reply and proposed plan below.

Summary answers (short):
- SCCs: Yes, Redwood executes EU SCCs for controller->processor relationships. We also have a UK Addendum (IDTA) template that we can put on DocuSign for signature.
- Subprocessors: Attached is the current register scoped to production inference (subprocessor_register.csv). None of the subprocessors hold customer PII in unredacted form by default; some provide managed GPU/infra in third-party regions (see register notes).
- TIAs/DTIAs: We have a condensed technical assessment that summarizes our mitigation controls and data pathways — attached as SCCs-exec-summary.pdf. Full internal DTIA artifacts are available under NDA; the summary should cover your review team's ask.

Proposed immediate deliverables and dates:
- Today (EOD): send the SCCs-exec-summary.pdf and subprocessor_register.csv (attached) — DONE.
- Thu 29 Apr: draft UK Addendum on DocuSign for Medixa review; include a short cover note explaining differences.
- Fri 30 Apr: deliver completed evidence checklist where items are marked DONE or PENDING with owner and ETA.

If your risk team needs a live walkthrough of the TIA summary, we can schedule a 30-minute call with Mina from our security team. Suggested times: Thu 29 Apr 10:00-12:00 ET or 15:00-17:00 ET.

I'll attach the three files now. If that timeline works, we'll follow up with the DocuSign link for the UK Addendum.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Legal
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Laura / Mina — quick note for the thread before we send DocuSign: please confirm the following so I can include in the cover note to Medixa legal.

1) UK Addendum: our standard position is to offer the UK IDTA/UK Addendum with signature on behalf of Redwood; exceptions require legal escalation. Confirm whether we should include an extra clause to reflect data residency controls for Medixa (they're a healthcare customer).

2) Subprocessor scope: ensure the register explicitly marks which subprocessors handle ephemeral inference cache (KV cache) vs. long-term storage — the distinction matters to their security reviewer.

3) TIA summary: Mina, can you add a one-paragraph callout about our KV cache segregation and redaction rules for inference inputs so it appears prominently in the summary PDF?

Thanks — I'll draft the short cover email and the DocuSign envelope once we have those clarifications.

-Karthik

Redwood Inference
